text:
elle: quick thread — affinity mapper for routing hosted/dedicated/private fallbacks.

elle: current behavior: when dedicated pool is full we silently route to hosted variant. customers with private deployments got surprised by telemetry + egress. we need a clearer contract.

sam: +1. can we define a tiny contract: request carries an "affinity" intent -> router evaluates allowed fallbacks. e.g., affinity=private:strict / private:best-effort / dedicated:prefer

raj: dedicated perspective: default must be no cross-tenant fallback. dedicated->hosted should only happen if customer explicitly enables it. otherwise return 429 or queue. (ops: @mia?)

mia: ops: agreed. also for burst behavior we should prefer queue or scale, not cross-tier. cross-tier introduces billing/acl edges. :warning:

kevin: product/latency tradeoff tho — some customers will accept degraded model variant rather than errors. can we support a 2-level policy: "fallback_mode": ["none","variant_only","cross_tier"]

elle: thinking API header + control plane config. header example:

```
X-Inference-Affinity: private;strict
X-Fallback-Mode: variant_only
```

and router config snippet (control plane):

```
router.affinities:
  private:
    default_fallback: none
    allowed_fallbacks: [variant]
  dedicated:
    default_fallback: queue
    allowed_fallbacks: [variant, cross_tier]
```

sam: important: "variant" fallback must be compatible model (arch + tokenizer). need a compatibility matrix in model catalog and a deterministic downgrade path.

raj: also req auth: fallback to hosted must be logged and require explicit billing consent. add an audit event: `fallback_decision` with fields {customer, from_tier, to_tier, reason}

mia: ops-bot: please add a metric for `router.fallbacks.count` broken down by from->to and fallback_type.

ops-bot: noted. creating ticket INF-1287 to add metrics + alert when cross_tier_fallback_rate > 0.5% of traffic for a customer.

kevin: UX: surface an admin toggle in console to allow cross-tier fallback per-customer, default off. docs must explain billing & data path.

elle: implementation concerns: router needs fast eval, avoid N+1 calls to model catalog. propose caching compatibility decisions in router and invalidating on model publish.

sam: also consider TLS/kms. private deployments may have models behind KMS. fallback to hosted might be blocked by key policies. router must consult "data residency" tag before fallback.

raj: good point. add rule: fallback allowed only if data_residency == target_residency OR customer_allow_residency_mismatch == true

mia: next steps: draft short RFC with API header, control plane schema, model catalog compatibility matrix, metrics, and console toggle. owner: @elle. timeline: 2 weeks for draft.

elle: thanks all. I'll start RFC + include a simple test plan (unit + e2e sim of saturation). ping me for review. :raised_hands:
